solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bird running wasn't emu

indicators.note: colours that run spread out of place, so the letters that follow are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of these two words, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: A birdwatcher insists the bird seen running was not an emu.
explanation.definitionFit: The mute swan is the common white swan of Britain, a large waterbird and so a kind of bird.

clue.text: Wretched driver missing last couple

indicators.note: missing the last couple means the final two letters of the word are dropped

blocks.note: a driver is a fore-and-aft sail on the mizzen mast, so the mizzen sail

explanation.surface: A miserable motorist has lost the last two of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driver' is not a motorist but a sailing term: the driver, or spanker, is a sail on the mizzen mast.
explanation.definitionFit: Mizz is an informal clipped form of miserable listed in Chambers, so it means unhappy or pitiful.

clue.text: One local detective, not fully employed

blocks.note: dialect form of one, as in 'a good un'
a busy is British slang for a police detective

explanation.surface: A provincial detective who does not have enough work to do.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Local' tells you the word for one is regional speech; busy is old British underworld slang for a detective.
explanation.definitionFit: Unbusy describes someone idle or with little occupation, which is having less than a full workload.

clue.text: Bacterium on the rise: conclude flourishing is without oxygen

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters are read from bottom to top

blocks.note: the word said to conclude a prayer
chemical symbol for oxygen
pert in its old sense of lively and in good health

explanation.surface: A bacterium described as rising and thriving in the absence of oxygen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without oxygen' looks like an anaerobic description; here 'without' means outside, so the oxygen symbol stands outside the word for flourishing, before the lot is turned upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Treponema is a genus of spiral bacteria, including the organism that causes syphilis, so it names a bacterium.

clue.text: Facing sit-in, desperately symbolic

indicators.note: acting desperately suggests wild disorder, so the letters are thrown into a new arrangement

blocks.note: all the letters of these words, hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: Confronting a desperate sit-in protest is a symbolic act.
explanation.definitionFit: Significant can mean carrying a meaning or signifying something, the same sense as symbolic.

clue.text: Weak old northern Scotch thistle heads — something like wilt?

indicators.note: the heads of words are their opening letters, so only the start of each is kept

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for weak
ould is the Scots and Irish dialect spelling of old
the opening letter of each of these two words

explanation.surface: Weak old Scottish thistles look to be wilting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wilt' looks like drooping, but it is the archaic 'thou wilt'; the answer is another archaic second-person verb form.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are old second-person singular forms of modal verbs used with thou, as in 'thou wouldst' and 'thou wilt'.

clue.text: A deviation off course arising continuously

indicators.note: in a down entry, arising means the letters are read upwards

blocks.note: taken as written
a yaw is a ship or plane swinging off its heading

explanation.surface: A ship drifts off its course again and again.
explanation.definitionFit: Away can mean without stopping, as in 'chattering away', so it carries the sense of an ongoing action.

clue.text: Begs to remove a valuation that's out of date

indicators.note: removing means a letter is taken out of the word given first

blocks.note: to pray is to beg or entreat
the letter to be taken out

explanation.surface: Someone pleads for an obsolete valuation to be withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a Spenserian spelling of price, which is why the definition stresses it is out of date.
explanation.definitionFit: Prys is an archaic spelling of price, the worth or value put on something.

clue.text: I am brought in for first part

indicators.note: being brought in means placed inside another word

blocks.note: pro means in favour of
contracted to I'm

explanation.surface: Someone says they have been called in to play the first part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' looks like a link word but supplies the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In a piano duet the primo is the upper, leading part, the first of the two players' parts.

clue.text: Chinese ready denial over hiding uranium

indicators.note: in a down entry, over means the word is turned upside down
hiding something means holding it inside, out of sight

blocks.note: nay is a refusal or no
chemical symbol for uranium

explanation.surface: A Chinese person willing to deny hiding nuclear material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ready' is not willing but British slang for cash, as in 'the ready'.
explanation.definitionFit: The yuan is the basic monetary unit of China, so it is Chinese money.

clue.text: Rapid drug treatment for flu

indicators.note: treating something works it over, so the letters are processed into a new order

blocks.note: speed is slang for amphetamine
the three letters reworked

explanation.surface: A fast-acting drug therapy for influenza.
explanation.definitionFit: Speedful is an old word meaning swift or quick, a synonym of fast-moving.

clue.text: Box of pills at home has run out

blocks.note: being in means being at home
R is the cricket abbreviation for run
O for out, as in a scorecard abbreviation

explanation.surface: A household's medicine box has run empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run out' reads as a phrase meaning exhausted, but the two words give a letter each.
explanation.definitionFit: An inro is a small Japanese lacquered case worn at the belt, traditionally holding medicines.

clue.text: Old embroidery, thoroughly elaborate

blocks.note: work was once the usual word for needlework or embroidery
up means completely, as in 'eat up'

explanation.surface: An antique piece of needlework that is intricately detailed.
explanation.definitionFit: To work up a sketch or idea is to develop it in detail, the verb sense of elaborate.

clue.text: Tumour formation goes on since receiving treatment

indicators.note: something receiving treatment is worked over and changed, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: all the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A tumour has kept growing since the patient began therapy.
explanation.definitionFit: Oncogenesis is the medical term for the origin and development of cancers, i.e. how tumours come about.

clue.text: One strange idea placing bird within lizard family

indicators.note: a strange version of something is an odd form of it, so the letters are scrambled
placing one thing somewhere sets it down in a chosen spot, here paired with the word within
within says the placed item goes inside the other letters

blocks.note: one as I plus the letters of idea, rearranged
a guan is a South American game bird

explanation.surface: Someone has the odd notion of putting a bird among the lizards.
explanation.walkthrough: The bird sits inside the jumbled letters, after the first I.
explanation.definitionFit: Iguanidae is the zoological family name of the iguanas, so it is a family of lizards.

clue.text: In revolt in South Africa, new village head

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the abbreviation that follows

blocks.note: ZA is the international code for South Africa
up in arms, rebelling
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: In a South African uprising a new village chief takes over.
explanation.walkthrough: The rebelling word and the new letter both sit inside the country code.
explanation.definitionFit: A zupan was the headman of a village community in Slavic lands, the local chief official.

clue.text: Forced change editor might make in agonizing on ad changes

indicators.note: a change of order means the letters are rearranged

blocks.clueFragment: change editor might make in agonizing
blocks.note: a British editor would put S for Z in this American spelling
these four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An editor agonizes over correcting an advert.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part is the phrase 'S for Z', exactly what turns agonizing into British agonising.
explanation.definitionFit: Sforzando is the musical direction for a sudden strong accent, the Italian term meaning with force.

clue.text: Before noon, tense doctor enters hall walking

indicators.note: entering a place means going inside it

blocks.note: aula is a Latin-derived word for a hall
Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
N for noon
T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Before midday, a nervous doctor walks into a hall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Before noon' wants to be AM, but 'before' only places the doctor-in-hall unit ahead of the letter for noon.
explanation.definitionFit: Ambulant means able to walk about, a synonym of moving on foot.

clue.text: Like a horse fool did shoe badly

indicators.note: doing something badly leaves it a mess, so these letters come out in a jumbled order

blocks.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: An idiot made a poor job of shoeing a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse has a single undivided hoof on each foot, which is what this term describes.

clue.text: One of the starlings, some millions wheeling

indicators.note: wheeling round means turning back, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: any as in 'have you any?'
M is the abbreviation for millions

explanation.surface: Some of a vast murmuration of starlings are wheeling in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Mynas are Asian birds of the starling family, so a myna is one of the starlings.

clue.text: Stop broadcasting right after signal

indicators.note: after sends the word for right to come second, behind the signal

blocks.note: a sign is a signal
off means right-hand, as the off side of a horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: A station stops transmitting straight after the signal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right after' reads as immediately after; 'right' is the word for the right-hand side, used of horses and of the side of a cricket pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: To sign off is to close a transmission, ending a broadcast for the day.

clue.text: Dye product that is protecting silk

indicators.note: protecting something means surrounding it, so one piece wraps around the other

blocks.note: i.e., Latin id est
satin is a glossy silk fabric

explanation.surface: A dye that is used to protect silk fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Isatine, or isatin, is a compound obtained from indigo, so it is a product made from a dye.

clue.text: Mushroom bloomed … it must have sun

blocks.note: to blow is to come into flower
taken as written
S for sun

explanation.surface: A mushroom has sprung up, and it needs sunshine to do so.
explanation.walkthrough: Blow in the sense of a flower opening ('full-blown') gives the past tense.
explanation.definitionFit: Blewits is an edible fungus with a bluish-lilac stem, a common wild mushroom.

clue.text: Regularly query Dutch language

indicators.note: regularly means taking letters at a fixed interval, every second one

blocks.note: the second and fourth letters
Du. is the dictionary abbreviation for Dutch

explanation.surface: A routine question about the Dutch language.
explanation.definitionFit: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan, also widely spoken in India.

clue.text: Enticed outside the City, the old make less

indicators.note: outside means one word goes around the other

blocks.note: drew as in attracted
EC is the postcode of the City of London

explanation.surface: Lured out of the City, the old earn less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The City' is London's financial district, whose postal district is EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Decrew is an obsolete verb meaning to decrease, so it is how old writers said diminish.

clue.text: Take away armoured fighting vehicles to break up?

blocks.note: first meaning: undo a mechanized force, stripping it of tanks
second meaning: Chambers also gives the sense to disorganize

explanation.walkthrough: To mechanize an army is to equip it with tanks and armoured vehicles, so the reverse removes them; the question mark flags the rarer sense of throwing into disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb reverses mechanizing, and Chambers lists it as meaning to disorganize, the same as breaking up order.

clue.text: Title for ruler, old uncle to the late queen

blocks.note: eme is an old Scots word for uncle
Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen Elizabeth II

explanation.surface: A long-gone uncle of the late Queen held a royal title.
explanation.definitionFit: Emeer is a variant spelling of emir, the title of a Muslim ruler or prince.

clue.text: Plan of Paris: in the centre, Seine river

indicators.note: the centre of a five-letter word is its third letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: the middle letter
the Dee is a river in Britain

explanation.surface: A map of central Paris shows the Seine river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plan' looks like a street map, but it means a scheme or notion, in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Idée is French for an idea or notion, so a plan as a Parisian would say it.

clue.text: Remain isolated, losing heart

indicators.note: losing the heart means the middle letter is taken out

blocks.note: stray as in occasional or scattered, e.g. stray cases

explanation.surface: Someone stays alone and becomes discouraged.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay is to continue in the same place or state, an exact synonym of remain.

clue.text: Moon's age at New Year, something agreed on by earth

indicators.note: one thing on another follows it, so the agreement is placed second

blocks.note: E for earth
a pact is an agreement

explanation.surface: The Moon's age at New Year is something agreed on by everyone on Earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' places the earth letter beside the agreement, before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The epact is the number of days in the age of the moon on 1 January, used to calculate Easter.

clue.text: A canned vegetable dish

indicators.note: canned means put into a container, so the article goes inside

blocks.note: a tin is a can
taken as written

explanation.surface: A vegetable dish that comes out of a can.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canned' does double duty, signalling the insertion and supplying the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A tian is a Provençal dish of sliced vegetables baked in layers, named after the earthenware pot.

clue.text: Have briefly to interrupt oddly distant millenarian

indicators.note: something done oddly is done in a strange way, so the letters are rearranged
to interrupt is to break into the middle of something

blocks.note: shortened to 've as in I've
the letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A believer in the coming millennium has short interruptions from a strangely aloof person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' looks like odd letters, but here it signals a rearrangement of the whole word.
explanation.definitionFit: An Adventist expects the imminent Second Coming of Christ, a millenarian belief in a coming thousand-year reign.

clue.text: Some feline pet adores this?

indicators.note: some of the following words means only part of their run of letters is used

blocks.note: letters running across the end of feline, all of pet and the start of adores

explanation.surface: A cat owner wonders whether the family pet will love this.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the plant too: cats famously adore it.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepeta is the genus of catmint or catnip, the plant whose scent cats find irresistible.

clue.text: Recurrent fuss about English concert halls

indicators.note: recurrent here means running back, so the word is read backwards
about means going around the letter that follows

blocks.note: ado is fuss or bother
E for English

explanation.surface: A repeated fuss is made about English concert venues.
explanation.definitionFit: Odea is the plural of odeum, a classical building for musical performances, i.e. a concert hall.

clue.text: Mountain goat territory involves height

indicators.note: to involve is to wrap up or enclose, so one piece holds the other

blocks.note: Ter. is an abbreviation for territory
H for height

explanation.surface: A goat's mountain range takes in high ground.
explanation.definitionFit: The tehr, more often spelt tahr, is a wild Himalayan goat-like animal living on mountain slopes.

clue.text: Watches county game's beginning

blocks.note: to eye something is to watch it
Down is a county of Northern Ireland

explanation.surface: Someone watches the start of a game in their county.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a bingo caller's phrase, called out to start the game.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Eyes down' is the call that starts a game of bingo, telling players to watch their cards.
